uncited: It builds on [3D Gaussian Splatting Differentiable Rasterizer](2813-3d-gaussian-splatting-differentiable-rasterizer.md) but adapts the projection and accumulation steps for X-ray geometry.

Partition the 2D image plane into non-overlapping tiles.
- **Precision:** The Jacobian calculation involves division by $t_z^2$ and $t_z^3$ (implicitly in the term $\frac{t_y}{t_z^2}$).
If $t_z$ is close to zero, numerical instability occurs.
- **Degenerate Input:** If $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ is singular, the inverse in the probability calculation will fail.
- **X-ray Geometry:** The definition of the intersection point $\mathbf{x}_j$ is not explicitly detailed in the source beyond being the "intersection 3D point of the X-ray landing on pixel p".
- **Time Complexity:** Linear in the number of Gaussians $N_p$ and the number of pixels, assuming efficient tile-based culling.
The sorting step is $O(N_p \log N_p)$ per tile.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N_p)$ to store Gaussian parameters and tile lists.
- **When to use:** When rendering novel X-ray projections from a radiative Gaussian point cloud.
- **When not to use:** For standard optical RGB rendering; when X-ray source parameters are unknown.
It is part of the X-Gaussian framework, which adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting for X-ray imaging.
